ads.headline: Carbon transmitter capsules
ads.body: Sealed capsule and contact set, from the electrical drawers. An older pattern than the telephone company carries, which is why we still have one. Ask at the counter.

ads.headline: Rubber protectant, service bottle
ads.body: Twenty-five cents, stopper included. Dresses the rubber washers in your fire-hose fittings. It does not replace a missing washer, certify the line or put out the fire. We have been asked.

ads.headline: Fire-hose coupling gaskets, ten cents
ads.body: A rubber washer of the fire-cabinet union's retained pattern, in a small pressed tin. It is the cheapest thing in the cabinet, and the only one that stops the water going sideways.

ads.headline: Soap flakes, scouring powder, matches
ads.body: Flakes twelve cents, twenty washes. Scouring powder ten cents. Kitchen matches five cents the box of fifty. Paint and sash cord also, if the matches go badly.

ads.headline: Silk flex for the man with a position
ads.body: Woven silk at a good price by the yard, rubber for the rest of you. Your visitors will not look at your furniture. They will look at your flex.

ads.headline: Valves by the six-sleeve
ads.body: Newark receiving valves in the printed sleeve, about a dollar the six. Keep a spare in the drawer and not in the window, where the glass tells the street.

ads.headline: One spare, with permission
ads.body: Bring the resident's permission and we cut one spare. The original stays with the resident. Blanks in brass and nickel on the board. Padlocks on the rail.

ads.headline: We have your key somewhere
ads.body: Hundreds of blanks on brass hooks, sorted by profile. Every one opens something. The locksmith would rather not say what, and he will want that permission in writing.

ads.headline: The Borough Record, two cents
ads.body: Queens County's paper of record, every morning, from the rack in the Arcade and the coin boxes on the kerb. Numbers, names and committee titles, in the order they occurred.

ads.headline: The Loud Speaker, one cent
ads.body: If it happened, we heard it. Half the price of the other paper and three times the sale. Read it before your employer does, and keep it from your mother.

ads.headline: Quell tonic, five cents the bottle
ads.body: Cold from the case at the News & Cigars counter. It quells. Our lawyer would like us to stop there, and so we shall.

ads.headline: A bar of chocolate, five cents
ads.body: The same size as last year, the man says. So are you, he says. Take it home, or eat it in the Arcade where nobody counts.

ads.headline: Milk, eggs, bread and valves
ads.body: Meridian milk, fifteen cents. Eggs, forty-five the dozen. White loaf, nine cents. Valves beside the cigarettes, in the sleeve. All from the one counter, before the first trolley.

ads.headline: Rat-trap cheddar
ads.body: Thirty-two cents the pound. Named for its use and its reputation. The rats of Queens have been known to write in. So far we have only their word.

ads.headline: Harukiya shoyu, twenty cents
ads.body: Sold at the bodega, twenty tablespoons to the bottle. We can tell you about the sauce. We cannot tell you anything about the rest of the Harukiya, and neither can they.

ads.headline: Peerless lager, twelve cents
ads.body: A lawful cereal beverage, and it has been described to the sergeant as such. The sergeant has had two and agrees. Peerless is sold by the bottle, without remark.

ads.headline: Fall River smoked sausage
ads.body: Thirty cents the twelve ounces. It keeps. Holloway's prepared mustard goes with it, twelve cents, and Astoria cream if you are expecting someone you wish to impress.

ads.headline: Yesterday's rolls, today
ads.body: Six for a nickel. They were fresh when you could not afford them. Gingersnaps a dime the dozen, dripping eight cents, and spent coffee grounds free to anyone who asks.

ads.headline: Coffee, pie and two receiving cabinets
ads.body: Sandwiches at the counter. Hot coffee from the twin urns. Pickled eggs in the jar. Two cabinets in the corner, which nobody has remarked on, and neither shall we.

ads.headline: Our carbonator has never been wrong
ads.body: Soda from the marble fountain, nickel taps, a row of syrups. The milk shake is mixed on green enamel. The customer has been wrong a number of times.

ads.headline: Soda at the druggist's
ads.body: Four stools at the marble fountain, halfway down the shop. It is the only thing we sell of which we can say with confidence what it will do.

ads.headline: Spices and bicarbonate of soda
ads.body: Cinnamon, nutmeg, cloves, bay, paprika, mustard powder, from the drawers. Bicarbonate five cents. Nobody has ever been cured of anything by our bay leaves, but the stew improved.

ads.headline: For cuts, carbolic and a clean rag
ads.body: Boil the rag. Keep the cut dry. If it reddens, send for us early. The show globes in our window are coloured water and are not for sale.

ads.headline: A photograph is an occasion
ads.body: Plates, paper and chemicals by the box. Everyone in Queens has a record of your voice. Nobody has a picture of your face. Come in while you have one.

ads.headline: Sets repaired on the premises
ads.body: Your set on our cradle, its back off and its valves standing. Scope and signal generator on the bench. The schematic is pasted in your lid, and we can read it.

ads.headline: Unredeemed articles for sale
ads.body: A violin, a sewing machine, a camera, surgical instruments, a mantel clock, a wedding ring in a small envelope. Each held its full term. Each with a number.

ads.headline: A used valve has seen things
ads.body: Second-hand valves on Jackson Avenue, at whatever they were this morning. They have one more evening in them, probably. Your overcoat is still here, and it asks after you.

ads.headline: Gas mantles: we have none
ads.body: We have no more of the old pattern, and neither has the company. A workroom that has spent its dozen should write to its management office, and then make them last.

ads.headline: Hear what the pipes are saying
ads.body: One contact microphone, hard-wired, with alligator clip and a hand-wound coil of shielded cable. By post only. They will say it whether you listen or not, so you may as well.
ads.offer: Send no money until it comes

ads.headline: Your shirts are still here
ads.body: Brown paper, string and a ticket. Some of these have waited since the war. We have kept them clean, which is more than can be said of the gentleman who left them.

ads.headline: You can smell our work from here
ads.body: Heels and soles on the finishing machine: brushes, drums, wheels and a belt. Loud, filthy, and the reason the street smells like this. Your shoes will come back improved.

ads.headline: Sixteen chairs, and no hurry
ads.body: Front room with palms and folding chairs. Charges explained beforehand, in writing. Your voice on a good clear record costs little. A photograph is extra.

ads.headline: Dictate it. It types itself.
ads.body: Speak your letter to the cabinet, and it comes out in clean type with the spelling better than yours. Second-hand from eleven dollars. Your chilblains are your own affair.

ads.headline: It answers when you are out
ads.body: Our answering cabinet takes the message and is civil to your creditors. It is often more civil than you. Your wife has asked if it can stay and you can go.

ads.headline: Ice at the door, by the hundredweight
ads.body: The block on your icebox, the tray beneath it, and the same horse as before. Our machines have not improved in any way. Neither has the weather.

ads.headline: Long-life receiving valves
ads.body: The same glass that lights the borough, with a longer life and a longer price. Ask your Arcade hardware counter. Sold in the sleeve; six hundred hands; two shifts.

ads.headline: The answering doll, three dollars fifty
ads.body: She says six words. The maker has examined her at Newark and finds nothing to correct. Should she say otherwise at your house, the proprietress asks you to bring her back.

ads.headline: Listening Act door notices, in brass
ads.body: The Act wants a notice posted at your door. Ours is screwed on properly, by a man who does this. Licence is your own business at five dollars a year.

ads.headline: The room consent book
ads.body: Fifty pages. Every party to the room signs before anyone says anything further. Husbands find it clears the air. Dogs may mark with a paw.

ads.headline: Your pipes will testify
ads.body: Our licensed adjuster listens to the burst and tells you when, where and whose fault. He will not mend it. Policies by the room. Ticketed under the Act.

ads.headline: Your parlour will back you up
ads.body: A record of everything said in the room, admissible in court. Your side of the argument, preserved. So is hers. We recommend you consider that before you buy.

ads.headline: The listening chair
ads.body: Upholstered ear wings, a shelf for the set, and a spring that has been sat on by two previous gentlemen. You can hear everything. It will hurt only where you sit.

ads.headline: Party-line manners, ten cents
ads.body: When to speak. When to stop breathing. What to do when you recognize the second voice. Forty pages, revised for the present state of the wires, and approved by no one.

ads.headline: Now truly portable
ads.body: Our new portable wet cell needs only two men and a hand truck. Go anywhere your friends will still have you. Acid sold separately. Trousers also sold separately.

ads.headline: Parts for Vantry sets
ads.body: The makers have been gone for years. Parts are not made. We have one screw, and it is on somebody's lien notice. Repairs by reading the lid, and prayer.

ads.headline: Vantry service sets, second-hand
ads.body: Works perfectly. Older than the tenant. Nobody knows what half of it does, and it does that perfectly as well. No repairs by the maker. No maker.

ads.headline: Record one ordinary Sunday
ads.body: Members seal their records in copper for the people of 1978. Dues modest. Meetings monthly in Jamaica. The committee welcomes guests, who may sit at the back.

ads.headline: Phonautograph blanks by the dozen
ads.body: Clean wax, in the sleeve, for records of Queens. We do not ask what you will put on them. Unwise members have ended up in a cupboard, voted down by two.

ads.headline: Bury it for 1978
ads.body: Copper case, soldered lid, room for thirteen mothers or one Mr. Abbot. Your descendants may hear you. They will have nothing else to do, and they will be sorry.

ads.headline: Records with the tone removed
ads.body: Meeting fortnightly at the Flushing Free Library. Where possible. Mr. Moss, pharmacist, presides. We do not say what the tone is. We have only taken it out, where possible.

ads.headline: Felt for under your bedposts
ads.body: Four pads, twenty-five cents. Does not quiet the Hum, which the company states isn't any concern of ours or yours. It only stops the bed from joining in.

ads.headline: Tune your flat to forty-one
ads.body: Strike the bar. Now it is your idea. No claim is made for this device regarding sleep, marriage, the light company or the source of any tone, which remains unknown.

ads.headline: Bring earplugs or a petition
ads.body: Wax earplugs ten cents the pair. Our petition counter is your own affair. Keeps out everything but the thing you were trying to keep out.

ads.headline: The home cycle meter
ads.body: For the householder who wishes to read the figure for himself. It will read forty-one. The makers do not say why, and the company states it does not concern the company.

ads.headline: Our load is unchanged
ads.body: Domestic current at the published rate. Your bill shows a credit, which the company does not call a refund. All other questions do not concern the company.

ads.headline: Three minutes, please
ads.body: Lift the receiver and an operator answers. Your party is available when the operator says so. Please do not address the animal at Position 43, or send her anything.

ads.headline: The sardine with a following
ads.body: Packed in oil, sold by the tin, and posted to no address in particular. Some of our customers do not give their names. We never ask. Neither does the cat.

ads.headline: Map pins by the gross
ads.body: For the gentleman following a certain station about the Sound. We sell the pins. We sell the string. The lines still won't meet. We do not sell an explanation.

ads.headline: We make no claim as to 1610
ads.body: Our sets receive all licensed stations on the dial. Should yours receive any other, the maker asks you to write to the Radio Division and not to us.

ads.headline: For the licence queue
ads.body: Corn plasters, ten cents. Bring your form. If you have no form you will be sent to the back and given one. Bring two plasters.

ads.headline: Rent is due at the box
ads.body: Rent payable at the post box. Enquiries are not answered. Notices are fixed with good screws. The company has no further statement, and no office in which to make it.

ads.headline: Postal cards by the hundred
ads.body: One-cent stamp, one card, and you have thought of another. Your family has asked us to stop selling them to you. We have told them we are very sorry.

ads.headline: Learn to read a schematic
ads.body: Every set made has its drawing pasted in the lid. Twenty lessons by post, and you are a repairman. There is still no cure for your cough, but you can record it clearly.

ads.headline: Have it said properly
ads.body: Ten minutes on good wax for a dollar. For wills, apologies and the location of certain papers. We attend at home. Bring your own doctor, if you still have one.

ads.headline: The inside-window scraper
ads.body: Nickel a piece. Takes the frost off your glass from the inside, as nature did not intend. Leaves you a clear view of the aerial you paid for.
